title: Your Eval Expires in Five Weeks: Rater Drift, Haiku 5.5, Math Dumps
summary: Anthropic's Haiku 5.5 cuts prices tenfold with a tokenizer and 100k-token catch, OpenAI dumps 722 machine-made math manuscripts, Anthropic ties cyber permissions to verified tiers, and a King's College study finds verified AI study podcasts help weaker economics students most. The deep dive takes a production interviewing agent to show how a new rater can hide real improvement, how a drift estimate tells you when your evaluation evidence has gone stale, and how to apply both to your own pipelines.
shownotes:
Claude Haiku 5.5: a tenth of the price, but a hungrier tokenizer, forced reasoning and a 100k-token price cliff; Sonnet 5.5 cache reads halved; API credits for Max and Team plans.
Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program: model permissions granted by verified identity tier, not by prompt.
OpenAI publishes 722 math manuscripts from an unreleased model; Lean-verified vs unformalized results, and the Fields Medalists' letter.
AI study podcasts with named human verification help weaker economics students most (Dang and Nguyen, King's Business School).
Deep dive: your eval has a shelf life. Rater effects, index masking, drift and the economics of evaluation cadence on a production interviewing agent (Zhang and Esposito).
